030package dev.visdb.seesaw.formatting;
031
032import java.text.DecimalFormat;
033import java.text.Format;
034import java.text.NumberFormat;
035import java.util.List;
036import java.util.function.Consumer;
037import java.util.function.Function;
038import java.util.function.Supplier;
039import java.util.stream.Collectors;
040
041import javax.swing.SwingConstants;
042import javax.swing.text.DefaultFormatterFactory;
043import javax.swing.text.NumberFormatter;
044
045import dev.visdb.seesaw.formatting.FormatterFactory.NullFormatter;
046
047/**
048 * Number field; this class has methods to assist in accessing a NumberFormat.
049 * Subclasses may create one or more formats for the FormatterFactory;
050 * Often subclasses use a single format for the FormatterFactory's Formatters;
051 * but they may use more than one and usually they will use the same parameters
052 * for precision. In any event, the edit format is assumed the most precise;
053 * the "get" methods in this class obtain the returned value from the
054 * edit format. The set methods will update all the formats in the associated
055 * factory and should be overridden if this is not wanted.
056 * <p>
057 * Note, the get/set methods do nothing when a Formatter's Format is not a
058 * {@linkplain DecimalFormat}.
059 */
060@SuppressWarnings("serial")
061public abstract class NumberField extends Field {
062  /**
063   * Take the supplied number format and configure it with defaults.
064   * A number format that does big decimal.
065   * @param f function that returns/creates a Format.
066   * @return Format with some defaults
067   */
068  public static NumberFormat createNumberFormat(Supplier<NumberFormat> f) {
069    NumberFormat format = f.get();
070    if (format instanceof DecimalFormat df)
071      df.setParseBigDecimal(true);
072    return format;
073  }
074
075  /**
076   * Error indicator for get*Param type of  methods.
077   */
078  enum Error {
079    /** Not DefaultFormatterFactory */
080    FACTORY,
081    /** Not NumberFormatter */
082    FORMATTER,
083    /** Not NumberFormat */
084    FORMAT,
085    /** getNullFormatter formatter is neither NullFormatter nor null */
086    NULL_FORMATTER,
087  }
088
089  /**
090   * Check if the param is an error.
091   * @param o check this
092   * @return true if error
093   */
094  public static boolean isAccessError(Object o) {
095    return o instanceof Error;
096  }
097
098  /**
099   * Indicators for each {@link Format} for each of
100   * a {@link DefaultFormatterFactory}'s formatter's param state.
101   * On a read option, the elements are the values which are read;
102   * on a write either null or error. A field may be {@linkplain Error}.
103   */
104  public record Params(Object defaultP, Object displayP, Object editP, Object nullP) {
105    /**
106     * Check if any of the elements is an error.
107     * @return true if any error
108     */
109    public boolean hasAccessError() {
110      return isAccessError(defaultP) || isAccessError(displayP) || isAccessError(editP)
111          || isAccessError(nullP);
112    }
113  }
114
115  /**
116   * Constructor.
117   * @param factory formatter factory
118   */
119  public NumberField(AbstractFormatterFactory factory) {
120    super(factory);
121    setHorizontalAlignment(SwingConstants.RIGHT);
122  }
123
124  /**
125   * Sets the value of the field to an initial state consistent with
126   * the AllowNull property. If not AllowNull then 0.
127   */
128  @Override
129  public void cleanField() {
130    setValue(getAllowNull() ? null : 0);
131  }
132
133  /**
134   * Sets the number of digits needed for integer part of the number.
135   * <p>
136   * <b>NOTE:</b> This does not preserve a previously set locale.
137   *
138   * @param precision - number of digits needed for integer part of the number
139   */
140  public void setPrecision(int precision) {
141    setFormatParam((nf) -> nf.setMaximumIntegerDigits(precision));
142  }
143
144  /**
145   * Sets the number of digits needed for fraction part of the number.
146   * <p>
147   * <b>NOTE:</b> This does not preserve a previously set locale.
148   *
149   * @param decimals - number of digits needed for fraction part of the number
150   */
151  public void setDecimals(int decimals) {
152    setFormatParam((nf) -> nf.setMaximumFractionDigits(decimals));
153  }
154
155  /**
156   * Returns the max number digits used for integer part of the number.
157   *
158   * @return the number digits used for integer part of the number, -1 if a problem
159   */
160  public int getPrecision() {
161    return getNumberFormatParam((nf) -> nf.getMaximumIntegerDigits());
162  }
163
164  /**
165   * Returns the number of digits used for fraction part of the number,
166   * from the editFormatter.
167   *
168   * @return the number of digits used for fraction part of the number, -1 if a problem
169   */
170  public int getDecimals() {
171    return getNumberFormatParam((nf) -> nf.getMaximumFractionDigits());
172  }
173
174  /**
175   * Sets whether the parse method returns big decimal.
176   * <p>
177   * <b>NOTE:</b> This does not preserve a previously set locale.
178   *
179   * @param val true to return BigDecimal
180   */
181  public void setParseBigDecimal(boolean val) {
182    setFormatParam((nf) -> nf.setParseBigDecimal(val));
183  }
184
185  /**
186   * During initialization set the precision for the specified formats,
187   * do nothing if precision is null.
188   * @param precision precision
189   * @param formats initialize these formats
190   */
191  protected static void initPrecision(Integer precision, NumberFormat... formats) {
192    if (precision == null)
193      return;
194    for (NumberFormat format : formats) {
195      format.setMaximumIntegerDigits(precision);
196      format.setMinimumIntegerDigits(1);
197    }
198  }
199
200  /**
201   * During initialization set the precision for the specified formats,
202   * do nothing if precision is null.
203   * @param decimals decimals
204   * @param formats initialize these formats
205   */
206  protected static void initDecimals(Integer decimals, NumberFormat... formats) {
207    if (decimals == null)
208      return;
209    for (NumberFormat format : formats) {
210      format.setMaximumFractionDigits(decimals);
211      format.setMinimumFractionDigits(decimals);
212    }
213  }
214
215  /**
216   * Retrieve a value from this' FormatterFactory's DisplayFormatter's Format.
217   * @param param function that access the param value
218   * @return the value from the NumberFormat or -1 if no NumberFormat
219   */
220  protected int getNumberFormatParam(Function<DecimalFormat, Object> param) {
221    Object p = getFormatParam(param);
222    if (p instanceof Integer i)
223      return i;
224    return -1;
225  }
226
227  /**
228   * Retrieve a value from this' FormatterFactory's DisplayFormatter's Format.
229   * The argument is like {@code (df) -> df.getMaximumIntegerDigits()} where
230   * {@code df} is a {@linkplain DecimalFormat}.
231   * @param paramF function that access the param value
232   * @return the value from the NumberFormat or -1 if no NumberFormat
233   */
234  protected Object getFormatParam(Function<DecimalFormat, Object> paramF) {
235    return getFormatParam(paramF, (ff) -> ff.getEditFormatter());
236  }
237
238  /**
239   * Retrieve a value from this' FormatterFactory's DisplayFormatter's Format.
240   * Does nothing if the formatter is not a NumberFormatter.
241   * The argument formatterF is like {@code (ff)->ff.getEditFormatter()} where
242   * {@code ff} is a {@linkplain DefaultFormatterFactory}.
243   *
244   * @param paramF accesses the param value
245   * @param formatterF access the formatter
246   * @return the value from the NumberFormat or -1 if no NumberFormat
247   */
248  protected Object getFormatParam(Function<DecimalFormat, Object> paramF,
249                                  Function<DefaultFormatterFactory, AbstractFormatter> formatterF) {
250    Object o = getNumberFormat(formatterF);
251    if (o instanceof DecimalFormat nf)
252      return paramF.apply(nf);
253    return o;
254  }
255
256  private Object getNumberFormat(Function<DefaultFormatterFactory, AbstractFormatter> formatterF) {
257    if (!(getFormatterFactory() instanceof DefaultFormatterFactory ff))
258      return Error.FACTORY;
259    if (!(formatterF.apply(ff) instanceof NumberFormatter nfer))
260      return Error.FORMATTER;
261    if (!(nfer.getFormat() instanceof NumberFormat nf))
262      return Error.FORMAT;
263    return nf;
264  }
265
266  private static final List<Function<DefaultFormatterFactory, AbstractFormatter>> formatterFL
267      = List.of((ff)
268                    -> ff.getDefaultFormatter(),
269                (ff)
270                    -> ff.getDisplayFormatter(),
271                (ff) -> ff.getEditFormatter(), (ff) -> ff.getNullFormatter());
272
273  /**
274   * Set the param in each of the FormatterFactory's Format.
275   * The argument is like {@code (df) -> df.setMaximumIntegerDigits(123)} where
276   * {@code df} is a {@linkplain DecimalFormat}.
277   * @param paramF function that writes the param value
278   * @return param status from each factory/formatter/format
279   */
280  protected Params setFormatParam(Consumer<DecimalFormat> paramF) {
281    // Note: if the same format is in more than one formatter,
282    // then it is adjusted more than once.
283    // Ignore the null formatter.
284    List<Object> l = formatterFL.subList(0, 3)
285                         .stream()
286                         .map((f) -> {
287                           Object rv = getNumberFormat(f);
288                           if (rv instanceof DecimalFormat df) {
289                             paramF.accept(df); // write the parameter to "df"
290                             rv = null; // all is well
291                           }
292                           return rv;
293                         })
294                         .collect(Collectors.toList());
295    return new Params(l.get(0), l.get(1), l.get(2), null);
296  }
297  // If it's important to avoid doing the same format more than once...
298  ///// // Track formats that are adjusted so they're only adjusted once.
299  ///// List<NumberFormat> formats = new ArrayList<>(3);
300  ///// // Want: "if (!formats.contains(nf))", but require identity.
301  ///// // Actually, it still works with equals, but weirdly so.
302  ///// boolean contains = false;
303  ///// for (Iterator<NumberFormat> it = formats.iterator(); it.hasNext();)
304  /////     if (df == it.next()) { contains = true; break; }
305  ///// if (!contains) {
306  /////     paramF.accept(df);  // write the parameter to "df"
307  /////     formats.add(df);    // keep track of "df"
308  ///// }
309
310  /**
311   * Get the param for each of the FormatterFactory's Format.
312   * <p>
313   * Reading all the values is primarily for testing.
314   * @param paramF function to access param
315   * @return param from each format
316   */
317  protected Params getFormatParams(Function<DecimalFormat, Object> paramF) {
318    List<Object> l
319        = formatterFL.stream().map((f) -> getFormatParam(paramF, f)).collect(Collectors.toList());
320
321    // The return for null formatter
322    Error nullFormatterError = null; // no error
323    switch (l.get(3)) {
324      case Error.FACTORY -> {
325        nullFormatterError = Error.FACTORY;
326      }
327      case Error.FORMATTER -> { // the null formatter should get this error
328        AbstractFormatter nullFormatter
329            = ((DefaultFormatterFactory) getFormatterFactory()).getNullFormatter();
330        // leave it as null unless...
331        if (nullFormatter != null && !(nullFormatter instanceof NullFormatter))
332          nullFormatterError = Error.NULL_FORMATTER;
333      }
334      case null, default -> nullFormatterError = Error.NULL_FORMATTER;
335    }
336
337    return new Params(l.get(0), l.get(1), l.get(2), nullFormatterError);
338  }
339}
